chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
Whoever keeps in view the distance of the journey remains prepared.
ai.seo_question: How does remembering the distance of the journey prepare a person spiritually?
ai.summary: In this maxim from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) links the psychological concept of 'preparatory anxiety' to spiritual readiness, suggesting that the conscious awareness of life's transient nature and the Hereafter's vastness acts as a catalyst for moral and practical preparation. This reflects the Shia emphasis on *muraqabah* (self-monitoring), where the 'distance' of death serves not as a source of despair, but as a motivating force to align one's deeds with the ultimate destination.

en.sayed-ali-raza: 280. Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, said:
Whoever keeps in view the distance of the journey remains prepared.
